label: AgMsv_1.815
cite_parts:
bhūtabhāvilayāt tasmād vartamānalayād api /
cinnātha eva devo 'sau kālam ābhāsayaty alam // [AgMsv_1.815]
quick_english: Therefore, through the dissolution of past and future, and also through the dissolution of the present, this god, the lord of consciousness himself, fully makes time manifest.

tokens.grounds: vocative-like epithet in compound sense; cit-nātha
demonstrative pronoun, sandhi form of asau

label: AgMsv_1.816
cite_parts:
tad asya kālābhāsākhyā citsvarūpasya saṃsṛtiḥ /
svabhāva[svābhāsa]garbhā bhāveṣu bhāvābhāvamayī svake // [AgMsv_1.816]
quick_english: Thus, for this consciousness whose nature is to manifest time, transmigration—containing the manifestation of its own nature—appears among beings as consisting of being and nonbeing within its own form.

label: AgMsv_1.817
cite_parts:
rūpe sthitiḥ pramātṛtvasamullāso 'bhidhīyate /
idaṃ na yad ahaṃ cāhaṃ yan nedam idam apy adaḥ // [AgMsv_1.817]
quick_english: Abiding in its own form is called the unfolding of knowerhood: 'this is not what I am', and 'I am what is not this', and also 'this is that'.

tokens.grounds: passive verb, sandhi form of abhidhīyate
relative pronoun, sandhi form of yat

label: AgMsv_1.818
cite_parts:
yan nedam iti citreyam abhāva[ābhāsa]syaiva mānatā /
parā pramātṛtā yāsau śuddhā tasyāṃ pṛthaksthiti // [AgMsv_1.818]
quick_english: The varied cognition expressed as 'this is not this' is the supreme appearing of nonbeing; but in that pure knowerhood there is no separate abiding of such distinctions.

tokens.grounds: relative pronoun, sandhi form of yat

label: AgMsv_1.819
cite_parts:
na mānam astīty atrāṃśe kiṃ tayā praviviktayā /
yas tu sāṃsāriko mātṛbhāvaḥ sarvo 'yam īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.819]
quick_english: In that isolated aspect there is no cognition at all, so what use is that isolated state? But every worldly state of being a knower is of this differentiated kind.

tokens.grounds: relative pronoun, sandhi form of yaḥ

label: AgMsv_1.820
cite_parts:
tatrābhāva[sa]sya mānatvaṃ sa ca kālaprasādataḥ /
tathā hi paripūrṇo 'sau sarvasarvātmarūpadhṛt // [AgMsv_1.820]
quick_english: There, nonbeing becomes an object of cognition, and that happens through the grace of time; for this perfectly full reality bears the form of all things and the self of all.

label: AgMsv_1.821
cite_parts:
kva mātā kva ca vā mānaṃ kva ca meyo 'vatiṣṭhatām /
mātrādīnāṃ hi satyatve na syād āpekṣikī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.821]
quick_english: Where could the knower stand, where cognition, and where the known object? For if knower and the rest were absolutely real, their status could not be merely relative.

tokens.grounds: object of knowing, sandhi form of meyaḥ
optative/imperative sense in rhetorical question, sandhi form of avatiṣṭhatām

label: AgMsv_1.822
cite_parts:
meyād eva ca mātrāder bhāvo jātu prakalpate /
anyonyarūpasyālābhe lābhe vā tadayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.822]
quick_english: The being of the knower and the rest is conceived only from the known; whether their mutual form is absent or present, it cannot stand independently because of their incompatibility.

label: AgMsv_1.823
cite_parts:
sarvatrātiprasaṅgāc ca sarvajñatvādiyogataḥ /
yugapac cāpy anullāsāt tattvasyānupakāriṇām // [AgMsv_1.823]
quick_english: This view fails because it would lead to overextension everywhere, would entail omniscience and the like, and because noncontributing factors do not manifest all at once.

label: AgMsv_1.824
cite_parts:
anyameyādijanite mātṛtvādau tadanyataḥ /
tadbhāvasyāpy anutpannasamatvenaiva saṃsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.824]
quick_english: If knowerhood were produced by some other known object, then its own arising would depend on something else again, and so it would remain as if unarisen.

tokens.grounds: compound anutpanna-samatva + eva with sandhi, instrumental

label: AgMsv_1.825
cite_parts:
tasmād pūrṇaś cidātmāsau śivaḥ svāṃśaṃ vikhaṇḍayan /
nāham ityādibhedāṃśa idam apy avakalpayet // [AgMsv_1.825]
quick_english: Therefore this full consciousness, Shiva, dividing its own aspect, constructs the differentiated part beginning with 'not I' and also the object 'this'.

label: AgMsv_1.826
cite_parts:
tadanyasarvapūrṇatvam aham ātmani tāvati /
tato 'nyato 'pi saṃhartā jāyate nāham ity api // [AgMsv_1.826]
quick_english: The 'I' takes to itself, to that extent, the fullness of everything other; and from what is other there also arises the withdrawing sense of 'not I'.

tokens.grounds: quotation marker, sandhi form of iti

label: AgMsv_1.827
cite_parts:
ubhau tau idam aṃśau cāpy apohati parasparam /
buddhistham idam aṃśaṃ svaṃ svāham aṃśe tirodadhat // [AgMsv_1.827]
quick_english: These two parts mutually exclude each other; the own 'I' conceals the 'this' part, which stands in cognition, within its own 'I'-aspect.

label: AgMsv_1.828
cite_parts:
āste na drāvayaty enaṃ vastrāvṛtaghaṭādivat /
tad eva buddhisaṃsthāt tu samayāgrathitād atho // [AgMsv_1.828]
quick_english: It remains and does not dissolve it, just like a pot covered by a cloth; that same thing, though tied by convention, remains established in cognition.

label: AgMsv_1.829
cite_parts:
idam antarasaṃghātād ahamaṃśavyapohinaḥ /
ahamaṃśād idantaughavyapohād aham antarāt // [AgMsv_1.829]
quick_english: The 'this' arises from inner contraction that excludes the 'I'-part, and the 'I' arises from within through exclusion of the whole mass of 'thisness'.

tokens.grounds: compound aham-aṃśa-vyapohin, genitive/ablative sense in context

label: AgMsv_1.830
cite_parts:
vyapohātsvāhamo 'nyānyāhaṃvyapohasya bhāsanam /
ṣaḍdevatāḥ śūnyarūpā yadāśritya pravartate // [AgMsv_1.830]
quick_english: From the exclusion of one's own 'I' and the exclusion of other and other 'I'-senses there arises manifestation; relying on which, the six deities of empty form proceed.

label: AgMsv_1.831
cite_parts:
tad evedam iti jñānaṃ vikalpa iti gīyate /
sa kālaḥ kalyate yena viśvaṃ nijakalodayāt // [AgMsv_1.831]
quick_english: The cognition 'that is indeed this' is called conceptual construction; and that is time, by which the universe is articulated through the arising of its own parts.

tokens.grounds: predicate noun, sandhi form of vikalpaḥ

label: AgMsv_1.832
cite_parts:
tad atrāṃśe ya eṣo 'sti bhāsāṃśaḥ svaprakāśakaḥ /
bhāvarūpatayā so 'yaṃ sarvānuprāṇanātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.832]
quick_english: In that part there is this aspect of manifestation, self-luminous in the form of being; that is the very nature which animates all things.

tokens.grounds: relative pronoun, sandhi form of yaḥ

label: AgMsv_1.833
cite_parts:
na mātāsau na vā mānaṃ na ca meyaṃ nirucyate /
yas tv asau śūnyatāyogād abhāvo rudradaivataḥ // [AgMsv_1.833]
quick_english: That is not defined as knower, nor as cognition, nor as known; but that aspect which, through connection with emptiness, appears as nonbeing has Rudra as its deity.

tokens.grounds: relative pronoun, sandhi form of yaḥ
contrastive particle, sandhi form of tu

label: AgMsv_1.834
cite_parts:
sa eva mānatām eti yadyogān mātṛtābhāvi[va]taḥ /
mānāc ca pṛthaṅmeyam ity evam upapāditam // [AgMsv_1.834]
quick_english: That very aspect becomes cognition; through its connection knowerhood is oriented, and from cognition the known stands apart. Thus it has been established.

tokens.grounds: compound mātṛtā-abhimukha/abhivata sense; read as mātṛtā-abhivataḥ
quotation marker, sandhi form of iti

label: AgMsv_1.835
cite_parts:
itthaṃ kālasya mānatvaṃ pratipede 'tra kaiś cana /
ye śrīmadbhavatītyākhyagurupādopasevinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.835]
quick_english: In this way, the status of time as cognition was understood here by certain teachers who attended upon the revered guru feet known as Bhavatī.

tokens.grounds: instrumental plural, sandhi form of kaiḥ

label: AgMsv_1.836
cite_parts:
tad itthaṃ puṃsi ciddharmavibhavāmodaśālini /
mātṛtvadāyi yat proktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ kañcukasaṃjñitam // [AgMsv_1.836]
quick_english: Thus, in the individual self—shining with the joy of the glory of consciousness's nature and receiving knowerhood—there is declared the group of six called the sheaths.

label: AgMsv_1.837
cite_parts:
tad ekaikasya mānatvaṃ ke cana pratipedire /
anye tv ekasya sarvānyasacivasyeti manvate // [AgMsv_1.837]
quick_english: Some have accepted that each one of them has the status of cognition, but others think that one of them functions with all the others as its assistants.

tokens.grounds: contrastive particle, sandhi form of tu

label: AgMsv_1.838
cite_parts:
anye kadāpi kasyāpi kathaṃcit kva canetyādi /
anye dvayor dvayor anye trikadvayaniyogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.838]
quick_english: Others say that sometimes, somehow, somewhere, some one of them operates, and so on; others hold that they operate in pairs, and others by combinations of a triad and a pair.

label: AgMsv_1.839
cite_parts:
anyonyānugrahād anye bodhenānyonyato 'pare /
anye tu guṇasāmyātmaprakṛtim eva mānatām // [AgMsv_1.839]
quick_english: Some say valid cognition comes from mutual favoring, others from mutual cognition, while others hold that primordial nature, whose essence is the balance of the qualities, alone is valid cognition.

tokens.grounds: sandhi bodhena + anyonyataḥ; instrumental and adverbial sense
compound guṇa-sāmya-ātma-prakṛti; object of viduḥ in next verse
abstract state of being a means of knowledge

label: AgMsv_1.840
cite_parts:
mukhyatvena viduḥ suptamattamūrcchādidarśanāt /
sa yatraiva pramātāyaṃ yataḥ supta iva sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.840]
quick_english: They regard it as primary because of what is seen in sleep, intoxication, fainting, and similar states: wherever this knower stands as if asleep, that is taken to be the knower.

tokens.grounds: verb governing prakṛtim and mānatām from previous verse
ablative of reason; compound listing states

label: AgMsv_1.841
cite_parts:
saivāsya mātṛtā mānameyayor apravedanāt /
anyonyam avikāryatvāt prasupte 'pi tathāvidhe // [AgMsv_1.841]
quick_english: That alone is his knowerhood, because in such deep sleep cognition and object are not apprehended and there is mutual unchangeability.

label: AgMsv_1.842
cite_parts:
kevalaṃ prakṛtiḥ seyaṃ jānāmīty abhimanyate /
tatra mukhyaṃ tu yan mānaṃ yatpuṃsaivānudarśanam // [AgMsv_1.842]
quick_english: In that view, primordial nature alone conceives 'I know,' but the primary cognition is that which is the seeing belonging to spirit alone.

tokens.grounds: verb of mistaken or reflective identification
locative adverb referring to that view
sandhi yat + puṃsā + eva + anudarśanam; compound-like fusion in text

label: AgMsv_1.843
cite_parts:
tac ca śuddhaṃ nirvikāraṃ sadasadrūpatojjhitam /
itthaṃ ke 'py abhimanyante sāṃkhyakañcukasaṃśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.843]
quick_english: And that cognition is pure, unchanging, and free from the forms of being and nonbeing; some hold this view by relying on a Sāṃkhya covering.

tokens.grounds: sandhi form of tat before ca

label: AgMsv_1.844
cite_parts:
vayyābhidhānasya guror gṛhe jñānopajīvinaḥ /
anye dhībhūmim evāhur draṣṭṛdṛśyoparāgiṇīm // [AgMsv_1.844]
quick_english: Others, living on knowledge in the house of the teacher Vayya, call the level of intellect itself the means of cognition, since it is colored by seer and seen.

label: AgMsv_1.845
cite_parts:
pramāṇaṃ pāramarṣeyāḥ kecit tadvṛttisaṃcayam /
dharmādikāṣṭasaṃkhyātaṃ dharmajātaṃ pare viduḥ // [AgMsv_1.845]
quick_english: Some followers of Paramarshi say valid cognition is the collection of its modifications, while others hold it to be the class of properties counted as eight, beginning with merit.

tokens.grounds: object or predicate in reported views
group name derived from a teacher or school

label: AgMsv_1.846
cite_parts:
anye 'haṃkāram evāhuḥ kecid dhiyam atho manaḥ /
kecid tritayam evedaṃ samaṃ sarvatra manvate // [AgMsv_1.846]
quick_english: Others say it is the ego-sense alone, some say intellect, others mind, and some hold that this triad functions equally everywhere.

label: AgMsv_1.847
cite_parts:
anye daśānām ekaikam indriyāṇām prapedire /
kecit samastāny etāni sarvatrākūṭavṛttitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.847]
quick_english: Others accept each one of the ten sense organs, while some accept all of them together, because they function everywhere without confusion.

tokens.grounds: demonstrative referring to the sense organs

label: AgMsv_1.848
cite_parts:
andhasyāpi hi tat kiṃcidrūpāyatanam asti yat /
vikāram ekaśrotraspṛg akṣāntarasamasthiti // [AgMsv_1.848]
quick_english: For even a blind person has some domain of form, which produces a change when it reaches the hearing sense while the other senses remain in the same condition.

label: AgMsv_1.849
cite_parts:
prabhātaṃ pravilīnābhranabhomaṇḍalamaṇḍitam /
ity ākarṇya parāṃ tūṣṭiṃ yāty andho haimane dine // [AgMsv_1.849]
quick_english: Hearing, 'It is dawn, and the sky is adorned with a cloudless expanse,' a blind person feels great satisfaction on a wintry day.

tokens.grounds: sandhi yāti before andhaḥ in next token contextually

label: AgMsv_1.850
cite_parts:
yady apy anumimīte 'sau śītavāraṇajaṃ sukham /
tathāpy asya svasaṃvittir na rūpānavabhāsinī // [AgMsv_1.850]
quick_english: Even if he infers the comfort that comes from the removal of cold, still his own awareness does not directly reveal form.

label: AgMsv_1.851
cite_parts:
anye tanmātrarūpāṇāṃ mānatvaṃ pratipedire /
cakṣūraśmis tv asaṃsparśa ityādividhiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.851]
quick_english: Others accept the subtle elements as the means of cognition, appealing to rules such as the claim that the eye-ray makes no contact.

label: AgMsv_1.852
cite_parts:
adṛśyatvaṃ cakṣurāder ata evopapadyate /
yoginaḥ praty adṛśyatvaṃ jātucin nopapadyate // [AgMsv_1.852]
quick_english: On that basis the invisibility of the eye and other senses is explained, but with respect to a yogin such invisibility is never explained.

tokens.grounds: compound cakṣus-ādi; genitive singular with plural sense

label: AgMsv_1.853
cite_parts:
anye tu sthūlabhūtānāṃ jyotiṣāṃ mānatāṃ jaguḥ /
meyasyāpi pramāṇatvam apare pratipedire // [AgMsv_1.853]
quick_english: Others declare the gross luminous elements to be valid cognition, while still others accept even the object of cognition as valid cognition.

tokens.grounds: genitive plural, possibly specifying elements or lights

label: AgMsv_1.854
cite_parts:
yato bhavati mātṛtvaṃ tatpramāṇam iti sthitiḥ /
tadghaṭādyaiś ca yat tasmāt te 'pi mānam iti smṛtāḥ // [AgMsv_1.854]
quick_english: The position is that whatever gives rise to knowerhood is valid cognition; and since a pot and such things do that, they too are regarded as valid cognition.

label: AgMsv_1.855
cite_parts:
laukiko vyapadeśaś ca naiva vastvanusārataḥ /
sa hīcchāmātrakḷptatvāt prāyeṇaivopacārikaḥ // [AgMsv_1.855]
quick_english: And ordinary usage does not follow reality, for since it is formed by mere convention, it is mostly figurative.

tokens.grounds: sandhi hi + icchā-mātra-kḷptatvāt; ablative of reason

label: AgMsv_1.856
cite_parts:
kathaṃ jānāsi bhoḥ so 'haṃ jānāmīti ca coditaḥ /
ghaṭenānena dṛṣṭena jānāmīty abhibhāṣate // [AgMsv_1.856]
quick_english: Asked, 'How do you know, sir?' and prompted, he replies, 'I know by this seen pot.'

tokens.grounds: sandhi saḥ before 'ham in next token

label: AgMsv_1.857
cite_parts:
tasmān meye 'pi mānatvaṃ na hi nāma na laukikam /
abhedavāde mūlasthe virodho 'pi na dūṣaṇam // [AgMsv_1.857]
quick_english: Therefore, even if cognition is attributed to the object, that is not outside ordinary usage; and in a root-level doctrine of non-difference, even contradiction is not a fault.

label: AgMsv_1.858
cite_parts:
ye tu pramāṇam āhus tatsāmagrīṃ tair api sphuṭam /
arthāder mānatābhīṣṭā sā saṅghe 'py anyathā kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.858]
quick_english: But those who say valid cognition is the totality of its factors clearly accept the cognitive status of the object and so on; if that status belongs even to the aggregate, how could it be otherwise?

tokens.grounds: compound artha-ādi; genitive singular with plural sense

label: AgMsv_1.859
cite_parts:
anye tu sarvasyaiveyattāttabhedasya mānatām /
kramoditāṃ hi sarvatra kvacic cāpy akramoditām // [AgMsv_1.859]
quick_english: Others hold that every distinction of every measured thing has the status of cognition, arising in sequence everywhere and in some cases arising without sequence.

tokens.grounds: sandhi sarvasya + eva + iyattā-tad-bhedasya; complex compound
object of manvate in next verse

label: AgMsv_1.860
cite_parts:
kvacit kramākramagrāsaparipūrṇatvabandhurām /
manvate tanmataṃ tāvad diṅmātreṇopadarśyate // [AgMsv_1.860]
quick_english: In some cases they consider it to be full with a complete grasp of both sequence and nonsequence; for now that view is shown only by a brief indication.

label: AgMsv_1.861
cite_parts:
prathamaṃ meyayogena jhaṭiti pratibhāsinā /
anyārthadṛśyabhiprāyapracchanenaiva sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.861]
quick_english: First, through sudden contact with an appearing object, there is simply an inquiry on all sides into the intent concerning another seen thing.

label: AgMsv_1.862
cite_parts:
mātṛtvaṃ caramaṃ tatra cakṣuṣaḥ pravijṛṃbhaṇam /
tato mano 'haṃdhīvargavijṛṃbhāntaḥsamujjvalam // [AgMsv_1.862]
quick_english: Finally there is knowerhood: first the unfolding of the eye, and then an inner brightness through the unfolding of the group of mind, ego, and intellect.

tokens.grounds: first member of compound in next token context

label: AgMsv_1.863
cite_parts:
tataḥ pauṃsnābhisaṃśuddhasaṃvidullāsaśālitā /
tataḥ kālakalārāgayatyavidyāniśāḥ kramāt // [AgMsv_1.863]
quick_english: Then comes the radiance of purified masculine consciousness, and after that the nights of time, limitation, attachment, impurity, and ignorance arise in sequence.

tokens.grounds: compound describing a state of consciousness

label: AgMsv_1.864
cite_parts:
anyathā vā samaṃ vāpi dvandvayogena vā triśaḥ /
sarvaśo vā catuṣpañcayogenāpy āṇave pade // [AgMsv_1.864]
quick_english: At the limited level, these factors may arise otherwise or together, in pairs or in threes, all at once, or even in combinations of four or five.

tokens.grounds: instrumental of a compound meaning joining in pairs
instrumental compound with enclitic api; sandhi noted in grounds
locative referring to the limited state
locative noun indicating a state or plane

label: AgMsv_1.865
cite_parts:
abhāvakartṛtāsaṅgasiddhitarkākhyasaṃśayāḥ /
tatrāpi nanu jāyante tattatkramavicitritāḥ // [AgMsv_1.865]
quick_english: There too, doubts arise concerning nonbeing, agency, attachment, proof, and reasoning, varied according to their different sequences.

tokens.grounds: compound describing the doubts as varied by order

label: AgMsv_1.866
cite_parts:
tatpṛṣṭe cāvikalpāsau śuddhaiśvaryāvabhāsikā /
vidyā pramāṇatām eti paryantapramitisthitau // [AgMsv_1.866]
quick_english: After that, nonconceptual knowledge that reveals pure sovereignty becomes the valid means of knowledge in the final state of cognition.

tokens.grounds: locative compound indicating what follows after that
sandhi of ca + avikalpā + asau; fusion noted in grounds
compound describing the nature of that knowledge
locative compound indicating the culminating cognitive condition

label: AgMsv_1.867
cite_parts:
tataḥ sadāśivodārajñānecchāśaktisaṃśraye /
sa mātā pūrṇatām eti śaktyantādhvasunirvṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.867]
quick_english: Then, resting on the noble powers of knowledge and will of Sadashiva, that knower attains fullness, fulfilled in the path that culminates in Shakti.

tokens.grounds: locative compound describing the support of that state
subject noun referring to the cognizing subject

label: AgMsv_1.868
cite_parts:
itthaṃ pūrṇaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ yataḥ samavabhāsate /
tadanyatamabhāgāṃśatirodhānaviyogajāḥ // [AgMsv_1.868]
quick_english: Thus full knowerhood shines forth equally; yet differentiated forms of awareness arise from not being separated from the concealment of some part of that fullness.

tokens.grounds: abstract noun indicating the state of being a knower
compound explaining the origin of differentiated awareness

label: AgMsv_1.869
cite_parts:
saṃvidaḥ sphuṭatānyatvabhedān niḥsaṃkhyatāṃ gatāḥ /
ata eva hy ajānānaiḥ śivaśāstroditāṃ sthitim // [AgMsv_1.869]
quick_english: The distinctions of clarity and otherness in awareness become countless; therefore those who do not know fail to recognize the state taught in the Shiva scriptures.

tokens.grounds: explanatory particle; sandhi form of hi
instrumental plural participle from root jñā with negation

label: AgMsv_1.870
cite_parts:
sphuṭāsphuṭādisaṃvitsu smṛtyasmṛtyādigocare /
sauṣuptādiṣu śīghratve yuktyāmarśādyasaṃbhavāt // [AgMsv_1.870]
quick_english: In clear and unclear awareness, in memory and forgetfulness, and in states like deep sleep, reasoning and reflection cannot occur because of their rapidity.

tokens.grounds: locative plural compound describing varieties of awareness
locative plural compound referring to states like deep sleep
locative abstract noun indicating quick occurrence

label: AgMsv_1.871
cite_parts:
manovadhānaṃ saṃskāro dharmādyadṛṣṭakalpanam /
ity ete hi sphuṭaṃ śabdā nātra ko 'rthas tatri ... mā // [AgMsv_1.871]
quick_english: Mental attention, mental impressions, and the postulation of unseen merit are merely words here; they do not provide a real meaning in this case.

tokens.grounds: accusative compound naming a proposed factor
nominative noun naming a proposed factor
interrogative pronoun; sandhi form of kaḥ
nominative noun with elided initial vowel
locative adverbial form as given in the text

label: AgMsv_1.872
cite_parts:
ūrdhvordhvatattvavrātasya mānatve ca nirūpite /
adharādharatattvāṃśo meyatām avalambate // [AgMsv_1.872]
quick_english: When the group of higher and higher principles is established as the measure, the portion of lower and lower principles takes on the status of object.

quick_english: There is no sequence here, for if there were interruption it would imply mediation; neither knowledge nor the intellect perceives that awareness.

vidyā vivektrī proktā hi buddhipṛṣṭasamāśritā /
prakāśātmavapur bāhyam akṣam ālocanātmakam // [AgMsv_1.874]
quick_english: Knowledge is said to be discriminating and rests on the intellect, while the external sense faculty, whose nature is light, consists in perception.

compound describing the function of the sense faculty

label: AgMsv_1.875
cite_parts:
saṃkalpārthaṃ manaḥ prāhur abhimantrīm ahaṅkṛtim /
niścetrīṃ ca dhiyaṃ tatra vidyāṃ cāpi vivecikām // [AgMsv_1.875]
quick_english: They declare mind to be for conception, ego-making to be appropriating, intellect to be determining, and knowledge there to be discriminating.

label: AgMsv_1.876
cite_parts:
tatraiva rañjakaṃ rāgaṃ kalāṃ śaktatvadarśinīm /
kālaṃ vyavacchit kartāraṃ niyatiṃ ca niyāmikāṃ // [AgMsv_1.876]
quick_english: There attachment is coloring, limitation shows capacity, time delimits the agent, and restriction regulates.

tokens.grounds: verbal or participial element as given in the text

label: AgMsv_1.877
cite_parts:
āmṛśantīm anyamātṛsādhāraṇyāvabhāsikām /
grāhyamaṇḍalatadgrāhinānārūpāvamarśinīm // [AgMsv_1.877]
quick_english: Maya is reflective, manifests commonness with other knowers, and reflects the sphere of objects together with their various graspers.

tokens.grounds: compound describing the function of maya
compound describing differentiated cognition under maya

label: AgMsv_1.878
cite_parts:
māyāṃ pūrṇatvasaṃbhogapracyutikṣobhakāriṇīm /
sadvidyāṃ pūrṇaviśrāntidāyinīṃ suśivātmikām // [AgMsv_1.878]
quick_english: Maya causes agitation and a fall from the enjoyment of fullness, while pure knowledge gives rest in fullness and has the nature of auspicious Shiva.

label: AgMsv_1.879
cite_parts:
jñānanirbharabhāvāṃśasvarūpaparimarśikām /
icchāśaktiṃ pramātraṃśapūrṇabhāvāvabhāsikām // [AgMsv_1.879]
quick_english: The power of will reflects a nature filled with knowledge and manifests the full being of the knower aspect.

tokens.grounds: compound describing the power of will
compound describing the power of will

label: AgMsv_1.880
cite_parts:
āśritya paripūrṇo 'yaṃ mātṛbhāvo vijṛmbhate ṝü /
prakāśālocane pūrvaṃ saṃkalpābhimate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.880]
quick_english: Relying on these powers, this completely full state of the knower unfolds: first illumination and perception, then conception and intention.

tokens.grounds: demonstrative pronoun with elided initial vowel
textual marker as given in the source
dual compound naming the first pair
dual compound naming the next pair

label: AgMsv_1.881
cite_parts:
niścayānudṛśau paścād vivekāsaṅgitādvayam /
kartṛtāsthāvyavacchedaḥ sādhāraṇyāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.881]
quick_english: Afterward come determination and subsequent seeing, then the pair of discrimination and nonattachment, followed by the delimitation of agency and the manifestation of commonness.

label: AgMsv_1.882
cite_parts:
nānāvimarśāprakṣobhapūrṇameyapravedanam /
pūrṇamātṛtvasaṃvittir bhairavībhāva eva ca // [AgMsv_1.882]
quick_english: The presentation of the full object stirred by various reflections, together with awareness of full knowerhood, is indeed the Bhairava state.

tokens.grounds: compound with nominative ending; sandhi noted in grounds

label: AgMsv_1.883
cite_parts:
itthaṃ ṣoḍaśadhā meyamayaṃ yāvat prakāśayet /
tāvad vijñānacandro 'sau prokto dvyaṣṭakalāsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.883]
quick_english: Thus, as long as it manifests the object-domain in sixteen ways, this moon of consciousness is said to abide in sixteen phases.

tokens.grounds: accusative adjective describing what is manifested
compound naming the subject; sandhi noted in grounds
demonstrative pronoun with elided initial vowel
compound describing the moon of consciousness

label: AgMsv_1.884
cite_parts:
anuttarā sthitiḥ pūrvam ānandeccheśanāny ataḥ /
udayaś conatāveśa iti ṣaṭkaṃ vyavasthitam // [AgMsv_1.884]
quick_english: First is the unsurpassed state, then bliss, will, and lordship, and after that arising, inclination, and immersion; thus a group of six is established.

tokens.grounds: compound listing three states; sandhi noted in grounds
nominative noun with visarga sandhi form
compound with initial ca fused in sandhi; fusion noted in grounds

label: AgMsv_1.885
cite_parts:
anuttarāt samārabhya jñānaśaktyantam īdṛśam /
icchaiva tu kriyāśaktim īśanena samāsthitā // [AgMsv_1.885]
quick_english: Beginning from the unsurpassed and extending to the power of knowledge, will itself is established, and together with lordship it is established in relation to the power of action.

label: AgMsv_1.886
cite_parts:
prakāśasthitileśāṃśaṃ gṛhṇatī ṣaṇṭhatāṃ gatā ṝü /
icchādi yac ca tatpūrvānuttarānandasaṃgateḥ // [AgMsv_1.886]
quick_english: Taking up a subtle portion of light and stability, it attains a sixfold state; and the series beginning with will does so because of its connection with the prior unsurpassed and bliss.

tokens.grounds: accusative compound describing what is taken up
present participle describing will or power
textual marker as given in the source
compound indicating the series starting with will
relative pronoun; sandhi form of yat

label: AgMsv_1.887
cite_parts:
tadādiśleṣayogena saṃdhyakṣaracatuṣṭayam ṝü /
tataḥ svarūpasaṃvittilābhād bindvādikā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.887]
quick_english: Through connection with that and what follows, a group of four juncture syllables arises. From that comes the attainment of awareness of one's own nature, and from that comes a state beginning with bindu.

label: AgMsv_1.888
cite_parts:
tataḥ samagrasaṃdarbhabharitākārarūpiṇi /
visargaḥ kila śākto 'sau vikṣepa iti yaḥ smṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.888]
quick_english: Then, in a form filled with the entire sequence, there arises the śākta visarga. This is indeed remembered as projection.

label: AgMsv_1.889
cite_parts:
visargasyaiva viśleṣa iti saptadaśī kalā /
kvacid aṣṭādaśī saiva punaḥ prakṣobhayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.889]
quick_english: The separation of visarga itself is called the seventeenth phase. In some cases that same phase is called the eighteenth, because of its connection with agitation.

label: AgMsv_1.890
cite_parts:
anuttarasyākārasya parabhairavarūpiṇaḥ /
akulasya parā yeyaṃ kaulikī śāktir uttamā // [AgMsv_1.890]
quick_english: Of the supreme akula, the supreme letter a in the form of supreme Bhairava, this is the highest supreme kaula power.

label: AgMsv_1.891
cite_parts:
sa evāyaṃ visargas tu tasmāj jātam idaṃ jagat ṝü /
tasya prakṣobhayogyatvaṃ prakṣobhakalanodayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.891]
quick_english: That very power is visarga, and from it this world is born. Its capacity for agitation is the arising of the stir of agitation.

label: AgMsv_1.892
cite_parts:
prakṣobhapūrṇatābhāvāt tadakulakramonatā /
iti ṣaṭkasvarūpātmavimarśāndolanoditam // [AgMsv_1.892]
quick_english: Because agitation is not yet full, there is a bending into the sequence of that akula. This arises from the swaying reflection of the nature of the sixfold.

label: AgMsv_1.893
cite_parts:
anuttarasvabhāvatvād ādyasyaiva vijṛmbhitam ṝü /
sa eva bhagavān antar nityaṃ prasphuradātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.893]
quick_english: Because it is of supreme nature, this is the unfolding of the first alone. That very one is the Lord, inwardly always flashing forth.

label: AgMsv_1.894
cite_parts:
antaḥsthasarvabhāvaughapūrṇamadhyamaśaktikaḥ /
svecchākṣobhasvabhāvodyajjagadānandasundaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.894]
quick_english: He has the middle power filled with all beings within, and he is beautiful with the bliss of the world rising from the nature of his own willed agitation.

label: AgMsv_1.895
cite_parts:
nityaṃ sphurati saṃpūrṇavisargarasasundaraḥ ṝü /
śivaśaktyoḥ sa saṃghaṭṭaḥ sneha ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_1.895]
quick_english: He always flashes forth, beautiful with the rasa of full emission. That union of Śiva and Śakti is called love.

label: AgMsv_1.896
cite_parts:
atraiva pūrṇavaisargapade labdhuṃ praveśanam /
lehanāmanthanetyādisaṃpradāyam upāsate // [AgMsv_1.896]
quick_english: Right there, in the state of full emission, they practice the tradition of licking, churning, and so on in order to gain entry.

label: AgMsv_1.897
cite_parts:
tathā hi madhyamāṃ nāḍīm adhiṣṭhāyākhilaṃ vapuḥ /
prāṇayat paramaṃ tejaḥ prakṣubdhāmṛtamadhyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.897]
quick_english: For thus, having taken its stand in the middle channel, the supreme radiance vitalizes the whole body from the midst of agitated nectar.

label: AgMsv_1.898
cite_parts:
visṛṣṭirūpatāṃ gacched yāty ānandacamatkriyām /
apūrṇā kevalaṃ sā tu pūrṇā tu bhagavanmayī // [AgMsv_1.898]
quick_english: It moves into the state of emission and reaches the wonder of bliss. When merely incomplete it remains limited, but when full it is wholly of the Lord.

label: AgMsv_1.899
cite_parts:
tena vaisargikī śaktir ekaiveyaṃ prajṛmbhate /
visarga eva prakṣubdhaḥ prayatnadviguṇatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.899]
quick_english: Therefore this single power of emission unfolds. Emission itself becomes agitated because of the doubling of effort.

label: AgMsv_1.900
cite_parts:
hakāro nāma viśveṣāṃ vyañjanānāṃ prasūtikṛt ṝü /
sa eva ca punarbinduyogāt svām eva bhūmikām // [AgMsv_1.900]
quick_english: The letter ha is indeed the producer of all consonants. And that same ha, through connection with bindu, returns to its own level.

label: AgMsv_1.901
cite_parts:
anuttarām āśrayate so 'haṃbhāva iheṣyate ṝü /
atraivāvarṇajaḥ kākhyas tadanyaś ca ivarṇajaḥ // [AgMsv_1.901]
quick_english: It resorts to the supreme level, which is accepted here as the I-sense. From that same locus arise ka, born of the letter a, and another born of the letter i.

label: AgMsv_1.902
cite_parts:
tata eva hi rephāṃśacchāyopādher ṛvarṇataḥ /
ṭavargas tata evātha dharāc chāyopadhikramāt // [AgMsv_1.902]
quick_english: From that, through the limiting condition of the shadow of the repha part and from the letter ṛ, arises the ṭa class. From that again, through dha and by the sequence of limiting shadow conditions, the next class proceeds.

tokens.grounds: ablative of compound repha-aṃśa-chāyā-upādhi with sandhi r

label: AgMsv_1.903
cite_parts:
tavargas tatparaḥ paścād uvarṇādyaralāś ca vaḥ /
ivarṇavargāc covarṇāt krameṇety ata eva hi // [AgMsv_1.903]
quick_english: After that comes the ta class, and then ya, ra, and la beginning with u, and va, arising in order from the i-class and from u.

tokens.grounds: ablative of compound i-varṇa-varga with sandhi c
ca + u-varṇa with ablative and sandhi

label: AgMsv_1.904
cite_parts:
antaḥsthā ity aśītāś ca ivarṇād dviprabhedaśaḥ /
śaṣasānāṃ samudbhūtiḥ śuddhopādhikalāyujaḥ // [AgMsv_1.904]
quick_english: Thus the semivowels are reached, and from the letter i, in two divisions, comes the arising of śa, ṣa, and sa, joined with phases of pure limiting conditions.

tokens.grounds: past participle from aś with sandhi ś
ablative of compound i-varṇa with sandhi d

label: AgMsv_1.905
cite_parts:
icchāyā eva viśvo hi prasavo bahudhā sthitaḥ ṝü /
ata eva hi sasthānabhāvo yuktatvam arhati // [AgMsv_1.905]
quick_english: For the universal emanation is indeed of will and is established in many ways. Therefore its having its own proper place is fitting.

label: AgMsv_1.906
cite_parts:
jīvasyaiveyam āśyānasthitir yonyatmikā yataḥ /
saivānuttaradevasya śaktir atra nirucyate // [AgMsv_1.906]
quick_english: This womb-like resting state belongs to the living being, because that very state is explained here as the power of the supreme god.

label: AgMsv_1.907
cite_parts:
tatraivantaḥsthatattvāni parāvāgbhūmikākramāt /
avarge śivatattvaṃ tu kādau hānte śivāntakam // [AgMsv_1.907]
quick_english: There, by the sequence of the levels of speech, the inner principles are arranged: in the a-class is the śiva principle, and in the group from ka to ha is the range extending up to śiva.

label: AgMsv_1.908
cite_parts:
iti saṃpuṭayogo 'yaṃ triṃśakārtho nirūpitaḥ ṝü /
evaṃ pūrṇānavacchinnā ciddevī syād yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.908]
quick_english: Thus this enclosing union, the meaning of the thirty, has been explained. If the goddess-consciousness is clearly full and unlimited, then it is so.

label: AgMsv_1.909
cite_parts:
sarvam asyāṃ bhaved eṣā sarvatra ca tathā bhavet ṝü /
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati // [AgMsv_1.909]
quick_english: All would be in her, and she would be everywhere. Whoever sees me everywhere and sees all in me has that vision.

label: AgMsv_1.910
cite_parts:
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa mametyapi tan muniḥ /
abhāṣatārjunācāryavacasā tatra tatra ca // [AgMsv_1.910]
quick_english: For such a one I do not perish, and he does not perish for me. The sage spoke this, citing the words of teacher Arjuna in various places.

label: AgMsv_1.911
cite_parts:
saṃvidātmā hi vicchinno yadi syāt sarvabhāvataḥ /
bhāva eva bhaved eṣa svalakṣaṇaghaṭādivat // [AgMsv_1.911]
quick_english: If consciousness, whose nature is awareness, were cut off from all things, it would become a mere object, like a pot defined only by its own particular mark.

label: AgMsv_1.912
cite_parts:
ataś ca saṃvitsaṃvittvahāner eṣā praṇaśyati /
palāyate hi cit sā ced vyavacicchedayiṣyate // [AgMsv_1.912]
quick_english: Therefore, from the loss of its nature as consciousness, this consciousness perishes; for if one seeks to cut consciousness off, it flees away.

label: AgMsv_1.913
cite_parts:
nijottamāṅgcchāyeva svapadākramaṇakrame /
yac ca sarvaṃ mayi proktaṃ na paśyati mahājanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.913]
quick_english: And the fact that the great mass of people does not see all things in me, though it has been declared so, is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head while walking.

tokens.grounds: compound with iva: nija-uttamāṅga-cchāyā + iva; sandhi noted in grounds

label: AgMsv_1.914
cite_parts:
sa sarvamadhyavartitvān mayi tāvat pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
evaṃ prakāśāniṣṭhatvād asyāsatsamatājuṣaḥ // [AgMsv_1.914]
quick_english: Because he abides in the midst of all, he is indeed established in me; yet, because he is not grounded in the light and treats it as unreal, he does not recognize this.

label: AgMsv_1.915
cite_parts:
praṇāśa eveti muniḥ provācobhayavartmanā /
eṣa vastukramas tāvad yo 'yaṃ saṃpuṭa ucyate // [AgMsv_1.915]
quick_english: The sage declared that this amounts to destruction by both paths; this, so far, is the order of reality which is called the enclosure.

label: AgMsv_1.916
cite_parts:
tata eva samastādhvakalitāsanasadmani /
saṃvid ādheyatāṃ prāptā punar ādhāratāṃ gatā // [AgMsv_1.916]
quick_english: From that very principle, in the abode of the seat that contains all the paths, consciousness attains the state of being supported and again becomes the support.

label: AgMsv_1.917
cite_parts:
uktaṃ cānuttare yāge punar evāsanaṃ /

\hspace{3cm} tataḥ /
atra tu pravivikṣūṇāṃ jñaptikramavaśān muniḥ // [AgMsv_1.917]
quick_english: And in the supreme worship the seat was spoken of again; therefore here, for those wishing to enter, the sage speaks according to the order of cognition.

tokens.grounds: desiderative participle of pra-viś, genitive plural

label: AgMsv_1.918
cite_parts:
ūcivān bhagavān eva viśvaṃ tan nānyatheti yat /
abhinnasaṃvitsvātantryaṃ bhāsate bhedavartmani // [AgMsv_1.918]
quick_english: The Lord has indeed declared that the universe is not other than that, because the freedom of undivided consciousness shines forth on the path of difference.

label: AgMsv_1.919
cite_parts:
upadeśyopadeṣṭṛtvavyavastheyaṃ pratāyate /
svātmaiva hi gurur devaḥ para ity abhimanyate // [AgMsv_1.919]
quick_english: This arrangement of the one to be taught and the teacher is extended; for one's own self is regarded as the teacher and as the supreme god.

label: AgMsv_1.920
cite_parts:
svodīritāni vākyāni paroktānīti manyate /
pratipādyaṃ ca yad vastu yena ca pratipādyate // [AgMsv_1.920]
quick_english: One considers statements uttered by oneself as spoken by another; and the thing to be taught and that by which it is taught are likewise taken as distinct.

label: AgMsv_1.921
cite_parts:
tat sarvam ātmarūpaṃ hi bhedenaivābhimanyate /
yathā svapnapadāvasthām upadeśaparamparām // [AgMsv_1.921]
quick_english: Indeed all that is of the nature of the self, yet one regards it as different, just as one experiences a lineage of instruction while situated in the dream state.

label: AgMsv_1.922
cite_parts:
ākarṇayaj jaḍo jantur anyoktam abhimanyate /
tathaiva jāgradgarbho 'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ samastakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.922]
quick_english: Just as a dull creature in a dream hears and regards what is spoken as coming from another, so too this entire ordinary activity contained within waking is regarded in the same way.

tokens.grounds: present participle of ā-karṇaya with sandhi before jaḍo

label: AgMsv_1.923
cite_parts:
ko bhedaḥ svapnajāgratsu tarhi syād iti cet punaḥ /
bhaṇiṣyate 'tha vā nāthe svatantre kin na bhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.923]
quick_english: If one asks what difference there would then be between dream and waking, that will be explained later; or else, what has not been spoken by the free Lord?

label: AgMsv_1.924
cite_parts:
evaṃ jñaptikrameṇaiva bhedo vidhyanuvādayoḥ /
sarvaṃ devo 'tha vā devaḥ sarvam ity ekam eva hi // [AgMsv_1.924]
quick_english: Thus the difference between injunction and restatement exists only by the order of cognition; whether one says 'all is God' or 'God is all', it is indeed one and the same.

label: AgMsv_1.925
cite_parts:
vastutaḥ kumbhaghaṭavad viśvaṃ paryāyamātrakam /
vācya eṣāṃ tvam eveti tac chrīnārāyaṇo 'bhyadhāt // [AgMsv_1.925]
quick_english: In reality the universe is a matter of mere synonymy, like 'jar' and 'pot'; what differs is only the expression. Therefore glorious Narayana declared to them, 'You indeed are that.'

tokens.grounds: demonstrative pronoun with sandhi before chrī
aorist of abhi-dhā with elided a

label: AgMsv_1.926
cite_parts:
nanv abhede kathaṃkāraṃ kḷptir vidhyanuvādayoḥ /
yo danturaḥ sa caitro 'yam iti danturam āditaḥ // [AgMsv_1.926]
quick_english: But surely, if there is non-difference, how can there be an arrangement of injunction and restatement? For example, 'this toothy one is Caitra' first restates the toothy one.

tokens.grounds: objection particle with sandhi before abhede

label: AgMsv_1.927
cite_parts:
anūdya caitra ityaṃśo yadi nāma vidhīyate /
tad danturo 'nyaś caitrāc caitraś cānyas tataḥ katham // [AgMsv_1.927]
quick_english: If, after restating him, the part 'Caitra' is enjoined as something else, then the toothy one would be other than Caitra and Caitra other than the toothy one; how could that be?

tokens.grounds: proper name in vocative-like citation form

label: AgMsv_1.928
cite_parts:
ghaṭaś caitra itīdṛkṣā na syād vidhyanuvādatā /
tasmād ya eva caitro 'sau sa dantura iti sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.928]
quick_english: A case like 'the pot is Caitra' would not be injunction and restatement; therefore the situation is that the very one who is Caitra is the toothy one.

tokens.grounds: relative pronoun with sandhi before eva

label: AgMsv_1.929
cite_parts:
vāstavī jñaptimātrottho vidhir vidhyanuvādayoḥ /

ajñātaparyāyapadasthitīn prati prayujyate pādapa eṣa bhūruhaḥ /
kumbho ghaṭaś ceti tathaiva bhaṇyate maheśvaraḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat tv iti // [AgMsv_1.929]
quick_english: The distinction between injunction and restatement is real in practice but arises only from cognition; it is used for those who do not yet know synonymous terms, as in 'this is a tree, an earth-grower' or 'a jar, a pot', and likewise in saying 'the Great Lord is all this world.'

label: AgMsv_1.930
cite_parts:
itthaṃ saṃpuṭayogena paripūrṇā hi yā sthitiḥ /
yasyāṃ saṃhārasṛṣṭyaṃśaśatāny antaḥsthitāny api // [AgMsv_1.930]
quick_english: In this way, by the union of enclosure, there is indeed a perfectly full state in which even hundreds of phases of dissolution and creation stand within.

tokens.grounds: compound: saṃhāra-sṛṣṭi-aṃśa-śata, neuter plural with sandhi
compound: antaḥ-sthita, neuter plural with sandhi

label: AgMsv_1.931
cite_parts:
tām eva bhāgaśaḥ ke cid upāsitumanas tayā /
ekādidviguṇatvotthacatuḥṣaḍdvādaśādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.931]
quick_english: Some, wishing to worship that very state part by part, do so through divisions arising as one, twofold, four, six, twelve, and so forth.

tokens.grounds: compound: upāsitum-manas with sandhi before tayā

label: AgMsv_1.932
cite_parts:
saṃviccakramayair bhedair bhindate vividhaiḥ kramaiḥ /
ekā saṃvid dvidhā saiva dṛkkriyātmā tridhātha sā // [AgMsv_1.932]
quick_english: By various sequences it divides itself through distinctions made of wheels of consciousness: the one consciousness becomes twofold as knowing and acting, and then that same consciousness becomes threefold.

label: AgMsv_1.933
cite_parts:
pronmeṣaśaktisācivyāc caturdhāpy atha gīyate /
cicchaktyānandarūḍhyā tu pañcadhāsau prabhāṣyate // [AgMsv_1.933]
quick_english: Then, through the assistance of the unfolding power, it is also spoken of as fourfold; and through ascent in the bliss of the power of consciousness, this same consciousness is declared to be fivefold.

tokens.grounds: compound ablative: pronmeṣa-śakti-sācivya with sandhi before caturdhāpy

label: AgMsv_1.934
cite_parts:
ṣoḍhā tu svaraṣaṭkoktasaṃviccarcāvicāraṇāt /
yāvad dvādaśadhā saṃvitsṛṣṭyādau tulyagocare // [AgMsv_1.934]
quick_english: It is sixfold through contemplation of the worship of consciousness taught as the six vowels, and extends up to twelvefold in the creation of consciousness and in domains of equal scope.

label: AgMsv_1.935
cite_parts:
ekaikaśas tryātmakatvāt traye vā cāturātmyataḥ /
sṛṣṭiṃ kalayate saṃvit tatrābhyeti ca raktatām // [AgMsv_1.935]
quick_english: Consciousness conceives emanation either one by one through a threefold nature, or in the triad through a fourfold nature, and in doing so it takes on redness.

label: AgMsv_1.936
cite_parts:
sthitināśaṃ kalayate kvāpi śaṅkāṃ prakalpayet /
tāṃ saṃhṛtya ca bhāvāṃśaṃ saṃhārāt svātmanaḥ punaḥ // [AgMsv_1.936]
quick_english: Consciousness conceives maintenance and dissolution, and at times it may give rise to doubt; then, withdrawing that doubt and the portion of being, it returns again through the withdrawal of its own self.

label: AgMsv_1.937
cite_parts:
saṃhartrītvaṃ carcayate tadantaḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ /
na drutaṃ na nirodhaṃ vā svasvātantryeṇa vāñchati // [AgMsv_1.937]
quick_english: Reflecting on its role as the withdrawer, consciousness considers merit and demerit within that state, and by its own freedom it does not wish for a quick outcome or for suppression.

label: AgMsv_1.938
cite_parts:
evaṃ bodhāṃśakaraṇamarīcīcakram ātmani /
grasamānā saṃharate pramāṇāṃśasthitān ravīn // [AgMsv_1.938]
quick_english: Thus, devouring within itself the wheel of rays made of the faculties and portions of awareness, consciousness withdraws the suns that stand in the part of measurement.

label: AgMsv_1.939
cite_parts:
tataḥ kalpitamātraṃśaṃ saṃhṛtyākalpite hṛdi /
tatsarvātītam apy antar anavacchinnadhāmani // [AgMsv_1.939]
quick_english: Then, having withdrawn the constructed part of measurement into the unconstructed heart, it takes even what is beyond all into the unlimited inner abode.

label: AgMsv_1.940
cite_parts:
nayet tan nayanadvārād viśvaṃ yāvat tathā nayet /
tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ ca kalayed ityādikramayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.940]
quick_english: One should lead that universe through the door of the eye, lead it in that way as far as required, and then conceive emanation again, following this and similar sequential practice.

label: AgMsv_1.941
cite_parts:
dvādaśāram idaṃ cakraṃ sarvadā parivartate /
yasyaitāḥ sthūlamātratvaṃ māsarāśyādisaṃpadaḥ // [AgMsv_1.941]
quick_english: This twelve-spoked wheel revolves at all times, and its gross form appears as the arrangements of months, zodiac signs, and the like.

label: AgMsv_1.942
cite_parts:
akramakramavaśād dviśas triśo bhūriśo 'tha vividhaiḥ kramākramaiḥ /
cakram etad uditaṃ vijṛmbhate meyamānamitimātṛbhakṣakam // [AgMsv_1.942]
quick_english: By the power of sequence and nonsequence, this arisen wheel expands in twos, in threes, and in many other ways, through various orders, devouring the object, the measure, and the subject.

label: AgMsv_1.943
cite_parts:
etaccakragatānantakiraṇārāsamāśrayāt /
cakrabhedo na saṃkhyātuṃ kadācid api śakyate // [AgMsv_1.943]
quick_english: Because this wheel rests on endless rays and spokes within it, the divisions of the wheel can never be counted.

tokens.grounds: fused form: etat + cakra + gata + ananta + kiraṇa + ārā + samāśrayāt
subject whose count is in question

label: AgMsv_1.944
cite_parts:
yathā hi varhiṇaḥ patre sitapītāruṇādikam /
pronmiṣan nimiṣac cātra bhāsate 'py atathātmakam // [AgMsv_1.944]
quick_english: Just as on a peacock’s feather colors like white, yellow, and red seem to open and close and shine, even though they are not truly fixed in that way, so appearances can manifest dynamically.

label: AgMsv_1.945
cite_parts:
tathānunmiṣitālīnasūkṣmasaṃvitsunirbharaḥ /
cakreśo bhāti nimiṣatpronmiṣadvṛtticitritaḥ // [AgMsv_1.945]
quick_english: In the same way, the lord of the wheel shines, full of subtle consciousness that is unopened and dissolved, and made variegated by the activities of closing and opening.

tokens.grounds: fused form: tathā + anunmiṣita + ālīna + sūkṣma + saṃvit + sunirbharaḥ
describes the lord of the wheel

label: AgMsv_1.946
cite_parts:
tat kasyāpi nimeṣeṇa kasyāpy unmeṣayogataḥ /
ekāracakrāt prabhṛti sahasrāraṃ vivartate // [AgMsv_1.946]
quick_english: Therefore, through the closing of some and the opening of others, the wheel turns forth in forms ranging from one spoke to a thousand spokes.

label: AgMsv_1.947
cite_parts:
tad asaṃkhyānam atha vāpy anyonyāśritagarbhakam /
na vā tac cakram atha kiṃ vyomaivaikaṃ vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.947]
quick_english: Is that wheel innumerable, or mutually nested within itself, or not a wheel at all—does one space alone expand?

tokens.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to the wheel/reality

label: AgMsv_1.948
cite_parts:
tad apy anantasaccakragarbhaṃ vāpi vibhāsate /
anantavyomagarbhaṃ vā mahāvyomaikam ucyate // [AgMsv_1.948]
quick_english: That too shines forth as containing infinite true wheels, or as containing infinite spaces, or it is called the one great space.

label: AgMsv_1.949
cite_parts:
yathā vyomaivaikaṃ kacati sitanīlāruṇatayā yathā caite meghāḥ punar atha tathā bhānti bahudhā /
tathā saṃvittattvaṃ kalanaparisaṃkhyāvirahitaiḥ svatantraṃ svākāraiḥ sphurati na ca te ke cana tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.949]
quick_english: Just as one space gleams as white, blue, and red, and just as clouds appear in many ways, so the autonomous principle of consciousness vibrates forth in many ways through its own forms, beyond construction and enumeration—and yet those forms are not anything separate from it.

tokens.grounds: ablative adverb indicating separation from consciousness

label: AgMsv_1.950
cite_parts:
iti tattvam idaṃ nyarūpayan mama nātho hṛdayasthitaḥ svayam /
pratipadya vicitrarūpakam gurusaṃtānaparamparāyitam // [AgMsv_1.950]
quick_english: Thus my lord, seated in my heart, having himself realized this principle of varied form, described it as transmitted through the successive lineage of teachers.

label: AgMsv_1.951
cite_parts:
tad amutra naye na ye prarūḍhiṃ pratipattuṃ kṣamatām upāśrayante /
nanu tatpratibodhanāya devo vividhāṃ maṇḍalakalpanām avocat // [AgMsv_1.951]
quick_english: For those who do not resort to the capacity to attain firm grounding in that doctrine, the Lord indeed spoke the construction of various maṇḍalas for their awakening.

tokens.grounds: locative adverb referring to that teaching

label: AgMsv_1.952
cite_parts:
bālo yadvat rekhayā varṇajāte svaiḥ saṃketair yojyate tatkrameṇa /
tadvanmudrāmaṇḍalair mantratantraiḥ pūrṇe svasmin yojyate dhāmny anarghe // [AgMsv_1.952]
quick_english: Just as a child is trained in the set of letters by lines and conventional signs in due sequence, so one is engaged, through mudrās, maṇḍalas, mantras, and tantras, in one's own full and priceless abode.

label: AgMsv_1.953
cite_parts:
atrāpi kiñcana vibhāti tadicchayaiva dūraṃ tathā savidham āśritatāratamyam /
asaṃspṛg apy atha niraṃśapadapratiṣṭham itthaṃ kriyāpaṭalago bahudhaiva bhedaḥ // [AgMsv_1.953]
quick_english: Here too something shines forth by that will alone as far or near, according to the gradation of those who take refuge; yet it remains untouched and established in the partless state. Thus the division belonging to the section on ritual action appears in many ways.

label: AgMsv_1.954
cite_parts:
itthaṃ pramāṇatābhāgi yat tattvaṃ hi nyarūpyata /
parāparā bhagavatī seyaṃ bhāti tathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.954]
quick_english: Thus the principle that was described as participating in valid cognition is that goddess, supreme and non-supreme, who shines forth in various ways.

label: AgMsv_1.955
cite_parts:
tad atraiva parāṃśo yaḥ sa mātraṃśo 'paraḥ punaḥ /
meyāṃśa iti tat pūrvam evāsmābhiḥ prakāśitam // [AgMsv_1.955]
quick_english: Right here, the supreme part, the knower part, and again the known part—this was previously made clear by us.

label: AgMsv_1.956
cite_parts:
mātraṃśo 'pi pare bhāge bahudhā yat sthitas tataḥ /
parāparatayodriktaḥ paro mantreśarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.956]
quick_english: Because the knower part is situated in many ways within the supreme part, it becomes predominant as supreme-and-non-supreme and takes the form of a lord of mantras.

label: AgMsv_1.957
cite_parts:
udriktāparabhāvas tu mantra ity abhidhīyate /
parāparas tu yo mātā samudriktaparāparaḥ // [AgMsv_1.957]
quick_english: But when the lower aspect predominates, it is called mantra; and the knower who is supreme-and-non-supreme, with the supreme-and-non-supreme balanced in predominance—

label: AgMsv_1.958
cite_parts:
sa vijñānākalaḥ proktaḥ prabuddhaparabhāvakaḥ /
aparodrekayogena sa eva pralayākalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.958]
quick_english: He is declared the vijñānākala, with the supreme aspect awakened; through the predominance of the lower aspect, that same one is the pralayākala.

tokens.grounds: technical designation of a knower level
technical designation of a knower level

label: AgMsv_1.959
cite_parts:
aparaḥ kila yo mātā sakalaḥ sa tu bhāṣyate /
parāparādibhedena tasyāpi bahudhā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.959]
quick_english: The lower knower is indeed called the sakala. Yet even he has a manifold state, distinguished by divisions such as higher-lower and so on.

tokens.grounds: by distinctions such as higher-lower etc.

label: AgMsv_1.960
cite_parts:
vicāryamāṇā niḥsaṃkhyān mātṛbhedāṃs tanoty alam /
mukhyatvena tu saptaiva mātṛbhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.960]
quick_english: When examined closely, this gives rise to countless divisions of knowers. But in terms of the main classification, only seven divisions of the knower are proclaimed.

label: AgMsv_1.961
cite_parts:
pramāṇāṃśe patanty eva teṣām eva svaśaktayaḥ /
vyāpārayogitaivaiṣā śaktitvam iti manmahe // [AgMsv_1.961]
quick_english: Their own powers fall within the sphere of the means of knowledge. We understand power to be precisely this fitness for activity.

tokens.grounds: in the domain of the instrument of knowledge
this very capacity to operate; sandhi: vyāpārayogitā + eva + eṣā
the state of being a power

label: AgMsv_1.962
cite_parts:
yac ca vyāpriyamāṇatvaṃ karaṇatvaṃ tad eva hi /
evaṃ ca śaktimacchakktibhedān mātṛpramāṇajāḥ // [AgMsv_1.962]
quick_english: For being active is itself being an instrument. In this way, from the distinctions between the possessor of power and the powers, the divisions of knower and means of knowledge arise.

tokens.grounds: the condition of operating or being engaged
the state of being an instrument
from distinctions between the possessor of power and the powers; sandhi: śaktimat + śakti + bhedān
produced from the knower and the means of knowledge

label: AgMsv_1.963
cite_parts:
caturdaśasvarūpaṃ ca prameyam iti bhāṣyate /
mātā mānaṃ ca meyaṃ ca yata ekaṃ prakīrtitam // [AgMsv_1.963]
quick_english: The object of knowledge is said to have a fourteen-fold nature. This is taught because knower, means of knowing, and knowable, though distinguished, are proclaimed as one.

label: AgMsv_1.964
cite_parts:
tataḥ pañcadaśātmaikam ekaṃ prakṛtipañcitam /
tatrāpy ekaikaśo bhede nijatattvasvarūpiṇi // [AgMsv_1.964]
quick_english: From that, the one reality is described as fifteen-fold, grouped in fives together with prakṛti. Even there, when divided one by one, each division takes on the nature of its own principle.

tokens.grounds: a single reality of fifteen aspects; sandhi: pañcadaśa + ātma + ekam
arranged in fives together with prakṛti
even in that case; sandhi: tatra + api
consisting in the form of its own tattva
